sections.title: A duplicate depends on the grain
sections.explanation: A person can submit valid applications for more than one role. Deduplicating by the wrong key can delete legitimate records.

items.label: Person
items.detail: One individual may appear in more than one application.

items.label: Application
items.detail: One application needs its own appropriate identifier.

items.label: Event
items.detail: Several interviews or updates can belong to that application.

items.label: Duplicate candidate
items.detail: A repeated application key needs inspection against the defined grain.

sections.takeaway: Investigate repeated keys and conflicting versions; do not silently delete rows just to get a tidy table.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Cleaning should leave an audit trail
sections.explanation: Keep raw data unchanged and make transformations explicit so someone else can reproduce them.

items.label: Preserve raw input
items.detail: Keep a read-only source copy and its provenance.

items.label: Transform a working copy
items.detail: Use declared mappings and date conventions.

items.label: Log each rule
items.detail: Record what changed, why and how many rows were affected.

items.label: Quarantine uncertainty
items.detail: Keep impossible or unresolved records visible for review.

sections.takeaway: A blank, zero and not-applicable value mean different things; do not invent a convenient replacement.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 2. Preserve source and make changes traceable

sections.title: Quality is several checks, not a blank-free sheet
sections.explanation: Keys, validity, completeness, chronology and reconciliation test different failure modes.

items.label: Check keys and fields
items.detail: Inspect uniqueness and required input coverage.

items.label: Check values and order
items.detail: Test allowed categories and plausible event dates.

items.label: Reconcile counts
items.detail: Explain changes to rows and distinct entities.

items.label: Document unresolved cases
items.detail: Preserve exclusions and their analytical effect.

sections.takeaway: A clean-looking dataset may still have incomplete coverage; report what remains unknown.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Should all rows sharing a candidate ID be deleted except one?
checkpoint.answer: Not automatically. Define the grain first: the same candidate may legitimately have multiple applications or events with different keys.

sections.title: Choose the operation that answers the question
sections.explanation: Counting records, adding quantities and joining reference fields are different spreadsheet operations.

items.label: COUNTIFS
items.detail: Count records satisfying the stated conditions.

items.label: SUMIFS
items.detail: Add an appropriate numeric field for those conditions.

items.label: Exact lookup
items.detail: Attach reference information using the correct identifier.

items.label: Manual check
items.detail: Reproduce a small result to verify the operation and ranges.

sections.takeaway: Check exact keys and unmatched lookups; a successful formula can still answer the wrong question.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Use formulas appropriate to the question

sections.title: A zero denominator is not a zero rate
sections.explanation: A percentage requires an eligible denominator in the same period or cohort. Missing references are another problem, not a reason to return zero.

items.label: Identify the population
items.detail: Apply the relevant cohort and period filters.

items.label: Count the denominator
items.detail: Check that eligible exposure exists.

items.label: Calculate if valid
items.detail: Divide compatible counts only when the denominator is positive.

items.label: Explain the exception
items.detail: Keep zero-denominator and missing-input states distinct.

sections.takeaway: Use an explicit undefined or not-applicable label and preserve the underlying counts.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: The summary must reconcile to its detail
sections.explanation: A pivot can aggregate duplicates or omitted categories as efficiently as valid data. Aggregation is not a cleaning step.

items.label: Fix the filter
items.detail: Use a documented population and period.

items.label: Include all categories
items.detail: Keep unknown classifications visible.

items.label: Compare total and detail
items.detail: Inspect counts as well as formula outputs.

items.label: Change a test input
items.detail: Confirm that the summary updates as expected.

sections.takeaway: Check that mutually exclusive, exhaustive groups add to the same filtered total, including Unknown where appropriate.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: If no offers were issued, is the offer-acceptance rate 0%?
checkpoint.answer: No. It is not defined for that group because the denominator is zero. Keep the counts visible and use a clear not-applicable label.

m2-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Pivots, distributions and analytical notes”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Mean and median describe different features
sections.explanation: A mean responds to every value; a median locates the middle ordered observation. Neither is automatically the right summary.

items.label: Mean
items.detail: Useful for an arithmetic average, but sensitive to extreme values.

items.label: Median
items.detail: Describes the central ordered case and can suit a skewed distribution.

items.label: Distribution
items.detail: Range and shape reveal what one summary can conceal.

items.label: Operational context
items.detail: A difficult genuine vacancy may be important rather than erroneous.

sections.takeaway: Investigate an extreme case before deleting it, and report sample size and context.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Mean and median answer different questions

sections.title: Segmentation can reveal or manufacture a story
sections.explanation: A group comparison needs consistent definitions, adequate coverage and a disclosure review.

items.label: Name the decision
items.detail: Choose the relevant group comparison.

items.label: Check comparability
items.detail: Align definitions, periods and role mix.

items.label: Inspect stability and privacy
items.detail: Avoid tiny cells and misleading percentage swings.

items.label: Keep the limitation
items.detail: Explain what the grouping cannot establish.

sections.takeaway: An overall change can reflect a different role mix rather than worse performance within each role.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An analytical note separates fact from interpretation
sections.explanation: Start with the observed count or rate, then state possible explanations and the evidence needed to test them.

items.label: Observation
items.detail: State the result, period, sample and definition.

items.label: Hypotheses
items.detail: List plausible explanations without presenting them as facts.

items.label: Needed checks
items.detail: Identify missing records or process-owner questions.

items.label: Proportionate recommendation
items.detail: Propose a bounded next step with an owner.

sections.takeaway: A descriptive result does not justify blaming a recruiter or employee.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: If overall time-to-fill rises, must every recruiter have become slower?
checkpoint.answer: No. Role mix, difficult vacancies, timing and other factors can change the overall result. Compare like groups and investigate before attributing blame.

sections.title: HR data quality and definitions: connect the question to evidence
sections.explanation: A reproducible synthetic workbook with preserved sources, definitions, cleaning decisions and reconciled summaries.

items.label: Question
items.detail: A reproducible synthetic workbook with preserved sources, definitions, cleaning decisions and reconciled summaries.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Use the original practice material with explicit provenance.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Explain a bounded recommendation and the evidence that could change it.

sections.takeaway: The app records reading and quizzes; external project submission, verification and marking remain with the institution.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep synthetic fixtures and authority boundaries separate
sections.explanation: The practice tables are independent examples, not linked real employee records. Use the original inputs and log every deliberate scenario change.

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Identify the fixture, grain, period and original source copy.

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Do not join independent populations as if they were one company dataset.

items.label: Permission
items.detail: Use synthetic inputs and the institution-approved submission route.

items.label: Honest context
items.detail: Do not report simulated interviews, approvals or outcomes as live events.

sections.takeaway: No real personal dataset, paid tool or live organisational access is required or authorised by this project.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reserve time for correction, not only construction
sections.explanation: The original work-plan table supplies the timing. This map groups the work into a review loop without changing those allocations.

items.label: Frame
items.detail: Read the decision and inspect source boundaries.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the required artefacts with traceable formulas or decisions.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Reproduce the headline and inspect assumptions and safeguards.

items.label: Review and revise
items.detail: Use peer or self-review and keep a change log.

items.label: Explain and submit
items.detail: Finish the recommendation, disclosure and evidence index.

sections.takeaway: A first draft is not a finished artefact; retain the comment and your response after review.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Organise the hr data quality and definitions submission
sections.explanation: These groups help you locate evidence; the full numbered submission checklist above still defines every required component.

items.label: Raw and cleaned layers
items.detail: Declare row grain, keys and provenance.

items.label: Dictionary
items.detail: Keep at least eight fields and four metrics with boundaries and rules.

items.label: Quality log
items.detail: Record duplicates, missing values and impossible-date decisions.

items.label: Checked summaries
items.detail: Show formulas or pivots, two hand checks and reconciled totals.

items.label: Privacy and limitations
items.detail: Explain access, safe sharing and what remains unresolved.

sections.takeaway: A public portfolio copy must be safe and clearly labelled; it is not a substitute for the editable institutional submission.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reconcile the declared application cohort
sections.explanation: The base fixture is a mature synthetic cohort of 24 distinct applications, split evenly across two sources. Keep counts traceable through cleaning and summary layers.

items.label: 24 applications
items.detail: Twelve per source under the declared application-level grain.

items.label: 12 offers
items.detail: Count offers within that same mature cohort.

items.label: 9 acceptances
items.detail: Keep acceptances separate from offers and joins.

items.label: 7 joins
items.detail: Joining is a later event, not a synonym for accepting.

sections.takeaway: A correct-looking pivot is not enough: preserve the raw data, define the application key and reconcile transformations before using the headline.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Follow the original rubric and its evidence standard
sections.explanation: The original block or capstone marks, performance anchors and institutional award conditions are unchanged.

items.label: Correctness and reproducibility
items.detail: Trace the method and results to the declared source and definitions.

items.label: Judgement and safeguards
items.detail: Show uncertainty, appropriate authority and safe handling.

items.label: Clarity, evidence and reflection
items.detail: Make claims inspectable and explain corrections.

sections.takeaway: These panels and animations do not calculate marks, approve projects or award an external credential.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Review the recommendation from a challenger’s view
sections.explanation: A reviewer should be able to trace a claim, test an assumption and understand which action needs another role’s approval.

items.label: Trace a headline
items.detail: Find the calculation or artefact behind the main claim.

items.label: Challenge an assumption
items.detail: Ask what missing evidence could reverse the action.

items.label: Check authority
items.detail: Name who is permitted to approve a consequential decision.

items.label: Inspect sharing
items.detail: Choose evidence that can safely appear in the public version.

sections.takeaway: Keep the actual review comment and your correction or explanation instead of claiming a review that never happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Explain assistance without outsourcing judgement
sections.explanation: Complete the original AI-use statement even when no AI was used. Tool help must not fabricate records, sources or experience.

items.label: Name tools or none
items.detail: State the actual assistance and permitted synthetic inputs.

items.label: Record your checks
items.detail: Explain accepted, changed and rejected suggestions and independent verification.

items.label: Own the work
items.detail: Describe your contribution, judgement and responsibility for the final claims.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload real employee, candidate, student or credential data to public AI tools; follow exam restrictions separately.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An extension tests an assumption after the core is complete
sections.explanation: The optional extension is not required for full marks. Keep the original work and distinguish a changed scenario from an observation.

items.label: Complete the core
items.detail: Finish the required evidence and safeguards first.

items.label: A deliberately unmatched key
items.detail: Show the failed lookup and keep it distinct from a genuine zero.

items.label: Compare and document
items.detail: Show what changed, which conclusion depends on it and what remains unknown.

sections.takeaway: More complexity does not improve a submission if the reasoning and safeguards cannot be reproduced.

checkpoint.question: Can repeated rows be counted as new applications just because the pivot total increases?
checkpoint.answer: No. Preserve raw inputs, define the application-level grain and inspect repeated keys. The published base cohort has 24 distinct applications; log any correction and reconcile summaries to the cleaned detail.
